title: Session-coalescing bucketed commit for retry-safe usage accounting
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: transient network errors, client retries, and partial streaming responses currently result in overcounting billed tokens in certain at-least-once ingestion paths. Existing solutions (nonce-based dedupe, replay tokens) mitigate many cases but leave gaps around long-lived streaming sessions, resumed uploads, and multi-path retries from proxies.

Proposal: introduce a session-coalescing, bucketed-commit protocol. Clients may provide an optional Coalesce-Session-ID header (opaque UUID) for logically grouped requests. The edge will map inflight requests with the same session id and matching canonical request fingerprint into a short coalescing window (default 500ms) for billing purposes. Token usage is recorded into temporary bucket entries keyed by (customer, session, bucket-epoch). A single consolidated commit for the bucket finalizes token counts to the canonical consumption ledger once a finalization marker or bucket timeout occurs. This enables at-most-once effective billing for bursts of retries and duplicate submission within the epoch while preserving low-latency accounting for non-duplicative traffic.

Key aspects: optional header (Coalesce-Session-ID), canonicalization rules for request fingerprints (model+params+prompt-hash+client-allocated sequence), bucket epochs (ms granularity), transient reservation credits for in-progress streams, and a reconciler job to convert buckets into ledger commits with audit trail links.
acceptance_criteria: Edge honors Coalesce-Session-ID and groups matching requests within coalescing window
Temporary bucket entries created and visible in staging billing DB; consolidated commit reduces duplicate ledger rows for bursts of identical requests by >= 90% in synthetic retry tests
Streaming partial token checkpoints append to bucket without creating final ledger charges until finalization or timeout
Rollout behind feature flag with fallthrough to existing idempotency paths
End-to-end tests and load tests demonstrate no regression in P50 latency beyond 10ms at the edge path under coalescing enabled
implementation_plan: API: define Coalesce-Session-ID header and canonical fingerprinting algorithm (edge spec)
Edge: lightweight coalescer component to dedupe/mux inflight identical requests into a single billing reservation
Billing DB: add bucket table (bucket_key, epoch_start, provisional_tokens, inputs_hashes, finalized boolean, audit_ref)
Reconciler: job to atomically commit buckets to consumption_ledger with idempotency guard and generate audit events
Runtime: streaming checkpoints write provisional token deltas to bucket; finalization path (end-of-stream or explicit commit) triggers reconciler run for that bucket
Observability: new dashboards for bucketed provisional vs finalized tokens, coalesce hit-rate, and failed reconciliation errors
Migration: back-populate short-lived buckets for immediate rollout; plan for longer retention for audits (30d)
Feature-flagged rollout: internal-only -> opt-in customers -> gradual percentage rollout -> all customers
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces duplicate billing surface for common client retry patterns and streaming resumes; works without changing existing client idempotency tokens. Cons: increases complexity in billing pipeline, creates short-lived provisional state that must be reconciled (more moving parts), and may slightly undercount during very rare cross-proxy split-brain scenarios until reconciler finishes. There is a small latency/CPU tax at the edge to perform fingerprinting and bucket mapping.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonical fingerprint function (determinism across equivalent inputs)
Integration test: simulate client retries and ensure single final ledger commit per logical request sequence
Chaos test: introduce split network conditions and verify reconciler converges and audit trail preserves all provisional deltas
Performance test: measure edge latency delta under 10k rps with coalescing on and off
Billing regression test: historical billing numbers should not materially change for non-retry workloads
rollout_steps: Create feature flag and gated rollout
Deploy edge coalescer in canary region with internal traffic
Enable streaming checkpointing for internal SDK clients and run stress tests
Enable for select beta customers with monitoring alerts on coalesce hit-rate and ledger divergence
Gradually increase traffic percentage while keeping auto-fallback to existing idempotency on reconciliation errors
Full rollout after 2 weeks of stability and audit sign-off
